chunks: Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hanaan, from Zurara, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We are Quraysh, and our Shiites are the Arabs, and the rest of the people are the 'Uluuj of the Romans.'

key_terms.شِيعَتُنَا: Our Shiites; referring to the privileged followers of the Imams.
key_terms.عُلُوجُ الرُّومِ: The 'Uluuj of the Romans; a term denoting the general populace or those outside the privileged circle, often interpreted as 'the rest of the people' or 'the commoners' in this context.
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: Quraysh; referring to the Ahl al-Bayt as the noble masters.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Uluuj al-Rum' in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates a spiritual hierarchy where the Ahl al-Bayt represent the noble 'Quraysh,' the faithful Shiites constitute the privileged 'Arabs,' and the general populace are likened to the 'Uluuj of the Romans.' This classification underscores the unique status of the Shiites as the inner circle of authority and knowledge, distinct from the broader Ummah. The metaphor draws upon historical tribal distinctions to illustrate levels of closeness to divine guidance.
